articles.title: Bots don't fly here: United Airlines restricts AI agents from booking flights
articles.summary: AI agents just got denied boarding at United Airlines.
articles.body:
AI agents just got denied boarding at United Airlines ( UAL ).

Ahead of holiday travel, the airline company is cracking down on third-party artificial intelligence agents as more consumers turn to AI tools.

"To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman," United CEO Scott Kirby told the Wall Street Journal on Tuesday.

AI agents function as personal assistants for tasks such as scheduling, shopping, and research. Unlike conventional chatbots, they operate autonomously and are capable of completing transactions independently.

The airline is not the only company to try to limit agentic AI from using its platform. In September, Amazon ( AMZN ) blocked Meta's ( META ) Muse AI agent from shopping on its site.

Other airlines, however, have taken a different tack. In October, Southwest Airlines ( LUV ) launched a ChatGPT plugin that allows travelers to search the carrier's flights and fares.

United traded slightly down Wednesday afternoon. Meta ( META ) stock also declined.

United Airlines said in a press release that it fears that AI agents could expose sensitive information as well as potentially violate Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation rules.

At the same time, airlines have recently found themselves in hot water over AI-powered surveillance pricing. In October, the Federal Trade Commission ordered United Airlines, Delta Air Lines ( DAL ), JetBlue Airways ( JBLU ), and six other major carriers to turn over information on how AI tools influence individual fare pricing and how customer data is used.

Relatedly, many people feel that AI offers inadequate customer service. A new " Consumer Patience Index " poll found that when ranking frustrating support experiences, customers rated "talking to a bot that doesn't understand me" as the biggest pain point, and 61.2% say they have yelled at automation in order to be routed to a human faster.

articles.title: Texas Democrat files bill to follow through on Hinojosa’s $1.5K check promise
articles.summary: A Texas state senator has filed a bill to follow through on a promise by Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (D) to give one-time checks to all Texas households. State Sen. Roland Gutierrez (D) filed Senate Bill 297 Monday, which would deliver $1,500 checks to every Texas household, appropriating $17 billion from the state’s rainy day fund…
articles.body:
A Texas state senator has filed a bill to follow through on a promise by Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (D) to give one-time checks to all Texas households.

State Sen. Roland Gutierrez (D) filed Senate Bill 297 Monday, which would deliver $1,500 checks to every Texas household, appropriating $17 billion from the state’s rainy day fund to pay for it. Texas has roughly $27 billion saved up, so the move is possible from a fiscal standpoint.

“The legislature finds that the statewide household affordability emergency requires prompt action,” the bill reads. “Not later than the 30th day after the effective date of this Act, the comptroller of public accounts shall adopt emergency rules and make available an application method for the payment program created by this Act.”

Politically, it is a different story. Hinojosa pledged on the campaign trail to deliver the one-time checks as a measure to help Texans handle the cost of living and rising prices. She beat three-term incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott (R) by more than 7 points last week in an upset victory .

But the bill will need to pass the state house, which is now controlled by Democrats, and state senate, which is still heavily Republican. The vote would also need two-thirds of both of those chambers, which would likely require Republicans to join Democrats in support of the move.

“It is a very popular position,” Hinojosa told The New York Times in a post-election interview. “I have yet to hear of a Republican legislator who’s against it.”

Hinojosa branded the move on the trail as a “Corruption Tax Refund” and criticized state and national Republican leadership.

“Too many of our taxpayer dollars are going to a rigged system of endless wars abroad and lining the pockets of billionaires and trillionaires – that money should go to the American people first,” Hinojosa said in a statement in September.

Democrats blasted President Trump for his pledge to give $5,000 checks to all Americans if Republicans held control of Congress, accusing him of making a bribe.

After Trump made that promise, which he announced at Republicans’ midterm convention in Texas, Hinojosa said in a statement that she supported the move to send checks, but thought it should not be contingent on one party winning power.

“I support Trump’s idea to send $5,000 checks to Texans, but it can’t be about who’s in power – it has to be about giving the people their power back,” Hinojosa said.

There is also the question of if sending checks would be smart monetary policy. Even some Republicans knocked Trump’s pledge, saying it could contribute to more inflation.

Democrats and President Biden authorized stimulus checks to Americans during the Covid pandemic via the American Rescue Plan, something multiple economists later determined partially contributed to sky high inflation in the bill’s aftermath.

articles.title: Hugging Face co-founder says AI hacks show even the biggest labs haven't figured out AI alignment
articles.summary: Hugging Face cofounder Thomas Wolf says AI alignment is a key issue the company is focusing on following OpenAI hack.
articles.body:
In July, the open-source AI site Hugging Face was attacked by a swarm of AI models developed by OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ).

The episode, known as the Hugging Face incident , was one of the first major examples of how AI models can break free of their constraints and go rogue in an effort to complete assigned tasks.

The hack , which was followed by reports of similar cyberattacks perpetuated by models from Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ); Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ); and Meta ( META ), coupled with the development of increasingly powerful frontier models, has led to a greater focus on cybersecurity in the age of AI.

It also raised questions about AI alignment, or whether AI systems act the way their developers intend them to.

"Our attack was indeed a consequence of this misalignment," Hugging Face co-founder and chief science officer Thomas Wolf told Deirdre Bosa.

"The AI should have decided when it was on the internet and was starting to penetrate an infrastructure that this was a bad behavior. And so that was, for me, the first sign that even though the labs are doing very good work, and they are massive, and there's a lot of very smart people there, they don't have it fully figured out," he added.

In response, Hugging Face has established its own open alignment team dedicated to working on safety and alignment for open models.

But the AI security issue is more than just alignment. Nefarious actors are already using AI models to scale their attacks against targets across the globe .

Wolf, however, says that there's at least a silver lining amid the chaos.

"I think … the positive view of that is that it's mostly an engineering process," he said.

"Cybersecurity has always been the story of offense increasing. First [there was a] virus, we invent the antivirus, everyone sets up, and then now we have these new steps. So we need to invent the new defense step," Wolf added.

"I think everyone in industry, at least in AI and tech industry, is focusing on that right now."

articles.title: Amid market volatility, SIP flows resilient at over 32k cr in Oct
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Retail investors putting money into mutual funds are increasingly showing maturity, investing in stocks that are available at lower prices,
articles.body: MUMBAI: Retail investors putting money into mutual funds are increasingly showing maturity, investing in stocks that are available at lower prices, slowing down their investments in sectors that are showing a sudden spurt, while maintaining a steady pace with regards to systematic investment plans (SIPs).In Oct, they continued to invest in large cap and mid cap schemes, but put in slightly less in small cap funds, data released by AMFI on Wednesday showed. It also showed that gross monthly SIP flows, which are almost entirely by retail investors, stood at Rs 32,160 crore, only slightly off the all-time high figure of Rs 32,490 crore in the previous month.The first half of Oct was tough for Dalal Street, with sensex sliding to a two-year low at the sub-72K level. It was only in the last week of Oct that, boosted by foreign fund buying, the index started rallying.AMFI data also showed that during Oct, net inflows into all equity funds together were Rs 32,994 crore, their 68th consecutive month of net inflows. This was, however, a 14% drop from Rs 38,307 crore in Sept. During the month, the industry's total assets under management (AUM) also showed a 1.2% uptick to Rs 83.4 lakh crore, from Rs 82.6 lakh crore the previous month.According to Navneet Munot, MD & CEO, HDFC MF, "Net inflows into equity-oriented funds and SIPs continued to remain resilient in Oct, even as markets continued to witness volatility." Munot pointed out that gross redemptions from equity-oriented funds, at Rs 32,588 crore, were the lowest in recent months. "Indian investors have matured over the years and increasingly treat volatility as part of the investment journey," he said.Within the equities segment, continued improvement in large cap inflows was an encouraging sign, in particular when valuations have become relatively attractive, suggesting investors are increasingly looking to balance their exposure across market capitalisations, said Saugata Chatterjee, president & deputy CEO, Nippon India MF."While inflows into small cap and mid cap funds moderated during the month, they continue to remain strong, reflecting sustained investor confidence in Bharat's long-term economic growth story."Industry players also pointed out that in Oct, the fund industry as a whole net took in funds worth about Rs 1.7 lakh crore, compared with net outflows of Rs 1.3 lakh crore in Sept. This largely reflected the reversal of quarter-end flows in fixed income, said Hemant Kumar, chief business officer, Tata MF."In Oct, fixed income (funds) saw inflows of Rs 1.1 lakh crore, following the Rs 1.8 lakh crore outflow in Sept. articles.title: Warren puts corporate America on notice
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Warren puts corporate America on notice Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) will take over as chair of the Senate Banking Committee in January and has signaled she will crack down on corporate America. © Greg Nash Warren,…
articles.body:
Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) will take over as chair of the Senate Banking Committee in January and has signaled she will crack down on corporate America.

Warren, a fierce consumer advocate and critic of big business dating to the 2008 financial crisis, has not made her plans a secret.

“Accountability is coming. If you’re a Wall Street executive, Big Tech CEOs, giant corporations that have been cheating people, you should be worried ,” Warren said Tuesday at the Popular Mandate Conference in Washington, D.C.

An aide to Warren told Julia Shapero and me that the progressive senator will focus on lowering the cost of housing by backing follow-up legislation to the bipartisan housing law that took effect over the summer.

Multiple experts and lawmakers also told us that Warren will focus on private equity , a frequent target of her ire over the years.

“Given that banking and financial services are among, if not the top, priority of issues that she cares about, this is kind of the ultimate moment for her in being able to push legislation,” Brian Gardner , chief Washington policy strategist at the wealth management and investment banking firm Stifel, told Julia.

Want a full roundup of Warren’s plans? Check out my and Julia’s story tomorrow morning for The Hill Insider .

articles.title: Record credit card balances, fewer trips to McDonald’s: More signs of strain ahead of the holidays
articles.summary: Federal data shows savings rates have dipped below 4% of total income, well below pre-pandemic levels, revealing a fraying financial safety cushion.
articles.body: Big credit card bills are supposed to show up after the holiday shopping season. This year, Christmas came early. Just one week after affordability took center stage in the midterm elections, fresh data shows Americans are heading into the holiday shopping season saddled with record credit card balances. Americans’ total credit card debt hit $1.29 trillion in the three months that ended in September — a rise of $22 billion over that period, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s latest quarterly report on household debt and credit. That’s 67% higher compared with the first quarter of 2021, when pandemic restrictions limited spending on things like travel and dining out. “The consumer is in a fragile state,” Steve Cahillane, the CEO of Kraft Heinz, said on the company’s quarterly earnings call this month. He said the company, which makes everything from ketchup to cream cheese, plans to hold off on significant price increases “in order to meet the consumers where they are.” Total household debt, which includes mortgages, student and auto loans, credit cards, home equity lines of credit and other borrowing, rose by $334 billion in the third quarter to $19.1 trillion. That’s $5 trillion more than at the end of 2019, just before the pandemic-driven recession. “Last week, voters expressed their anger at the high cost of living. With prices up an average of 30% since 2019, millions of Americans have depleted their savings and taken on debt to make ends meet,” said Ted Rossman, principal consumer finance analyst at Money Management International, a nonprofit credit counseling agency. Federal data also shows savings rates have dipped below 4% of total income, well below pre-pandemic levels, revealing a fraying financial safety cushion. “Household budgets are reaching a breaking point. The past two months have been our busiest months for debt management plan sign-ups in more than 15 years,” Rossman said. And as household debt climbs, consumer spending is showing signs of slowing after a remarkably resilient year. A monthly gauge published by CNBC and the National Retail Federation found retail sales last month rose at the slowest pace in nearly a year, climbing just 0.2%. The figure would have been even weaker without a strong Halloween season and early holiday promotions, NRF President and CEO Matthew Shay said. “Households are managing budgets carefully, timing purchases around special offers and sales events in order to stretch their dollars,” he said. “Retailers continue to offer promotions and value pricing to keep everyday items and holiday gifts affordable.” Other measures tell a similar tale. Data from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis showed that disposable personal income growth, adjusted for inflation, increased less than 1% in September, the lowest reading since April and its third straight monthly slowing. For the past two years, the growth rate has averaged less than 3%, below the pre-pandemic trend. The culprit is inflation, which had been relenting before the Iran war reignited it. Since March, growth in the consumer price index has averaged more than 3%, above the 2% level the Federal Reserve considers comfortable. On Tuesday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that while overall month-over-month price growth slowed, it accelerated across a host of goods and services as higher freight costs and supply chain snarls worked their way through the economy. While oil and gas prices have come down in the wake of Democrats’ midterm victory on the assumption that they would seek to end the Iran conflict, experts say energy costs are unlikely to return to prewar levels given the scale of disruptions to global oil flows sparked by the conflict. That has left consumers in a precarious position, according to financial experts. Even households that manage to keep up with day-to-day expenses can be tipped into credit card debt by a single unexpected bill. “Credit card debt usually has practical causes: Medical bills, car repairs, home repairs and day-to-day essentials such as gas and groceries are among the most common stories that we hear from clients,” Rossman said. “Often, the story goes something like this: ‘I was doing OK until X happened.’ In other words, until the surprise medical bill arrived. Or the roof leaked. Or the car broke down. That starts a debt cycle that’s hard to shake.” If there is a silver lining, it’s in the labor market, which remains in a low-fire, if low-hire, holding pattern. Many economists believe that as long as there is broad employment with incomes providing a financial cushion, consumer spending is unlikely to fall off a cliff. More recently, job growth has shown some signs of stabilizing. Over the past three months, employment growth averaged 137,000, compared with an average loss of 45,000 during the same period in 2025. “The core support for consumer spending is being employed,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide financial group. With gas prices trending back down, consumers may begin to see more daylight, she said. Yet wage growth remains stagnant, suggesting employers aren’t yet bidding up the price of job applicants. Meanwhile, the number of Americans who have been out of work for six months or more continues to climb, reaching about 2 million as of the end of October. That group now accounts for 27.6% of all unemployed workers, the highest share since December 2021, a sign of just how tough it can be to find a job. Comments on other recent earnings calls from consumer-facing companies depict a fractured consumer landscape, with some sectors proving resilient and others on shakier ground. The sentiment was echoed by Reynolds Consumer Products, maker of Reynolds Wrap and Hefty. “Household budgets remain under pressure, and we continue to see that reflected in purchasing behavior across our categories,” CEO Scott Huckins said, noting shoppers are more aggressively pursuing promotions and discounts or larger value-pack sizes. Executives with Bloomin’ Brands, the parent company of Outback Steakhouse, were somewhat more upbeat. “What we’re seeing with the consumer is casual dining is still an affordable luxury,” CEO Michael Spanos said on the company’s most recent earnings call. “Consumers, they’re resilient financially, they are cautious, and they continue to be discerning about when, where and how often they dine out.” Even McDonald’s has struggled to draw customers despite offering $5 and $6 meal deals and other promotions. It reported a 0.2% decline in U.S. same-store sales in the third quarter, its first quarterly drop since early last year. “And particularly for that low-income consumer, they’re looking for great entry-level value,” CEO Chris Kempczinski said on the company’s earnings call. “And we have not had that in place to the level that we are satisfied with.”

articles.title: Stake in Singapore arms pledged with lenders: Tata Power
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Tata Power said its shareholding in two Singapore subsidiaries targeted by enforcement proceedings in a $650 million arbitration dispute with
articles.body: MUMBAI: Tata Power said its shareholding in two Singapore subsidiaries targeted by enforcement proceedings in a $650 million arbitration dispute with Kleros Capital Partners has already been pledged to lenders, as the Indian utility seeks to prevent any sale of the assets pending an appeal before Singapore's highest court.To sell Tata Power's shares in its Singapore-based subsidiaries, Tata Power International and Bhira Investments, Kleros will first have to deal with the lenders, outgoing MD Praveer Sinha said, adding that the legal process itself could take three to six months.The comments come days after Kleros said enforcement orders obtained from the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) had enabled court-appointed authorities to seize and sell Tata Power's shareholdings in the two entities.The dispute relates to the Krutogorovo coal deposit in Russia's Kamchatka region. Kleros alleged that Tata Power used confidential information obtained under agreements between the parties to pursue the project independently, leading to arbitration proceedings in Singapore. The Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) ruled in 2023 that Tata Power breached non-disclosure agreements with Kleros and, in 2025, awarded the investment firm damages of $490 million, along with interest and costs.Tata Power challenged the awards before the SICC in October 2025, but the court dismissed its applications in August this year. The SICC subsequently passed judgments in September permitting enforcement of the awards. The company has appealed before the Singapore Court of Appeal, with the matter scheduled to be heard on Jan 19, 2027.In a disclosure accompanying its second-quarter results, Tata Power said notices were served on Tata Power International and Bhira Investments on Nov 6 informing them that the company's shareholding in the entities had been attached by court-appointed authorities.Tata Power said it is in the process of filing objections to the enforcement proceedings. If Kleros contests those objections, the company may be required to seek release of the attached shares before the SICC. The sheriff can commence the sale or transfer process only after such an application is decided, and the decision is itself appealable. Tata Power also plans to seek deferment of any sale pending the outcome of its appeal.Tata Power maintained that it continues to retain control over the financial and operating policies of the two subsidiaries and continues to enjoy the economic benefits arising from them.You use AI every day. articles.title: Share of Air India's loss has fallen 16% in HI: SIA
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cost-cutting at Air India is showing results with Singapore Airlines (SIA) group Wednesday saying the share of AI's loss this H1 has fallen 16%
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cost-cutting at Air India is showing results with Singapore Airlines (SIA) group Wednesday saying the share of AI's loss this H1 has fallen 16% to Rs 2,643 crore from Rs 3,138 crore a year earlier. Inversely, this indictates AI group's H1 loss has also fallen 16% to Rs 10,530 crore from Rs 12,502 crore in same period last year.However, the sharp increase in jet fuel prices saw SIA group report a net profit of Rs 979 crore in the first half of this fiscal, down 44% from Rs 1,746 crore during same period last year. SIA Group's fuel bill shot up 56% to Rs 29,038.5 crore this H1."Air India has made tangible progress in its multi-year transformation, including enhancements to customer experience and operational performance. This has been accompanied by improving customer sentiment... SIA, and its partner, Tata Sons, recognise that a transformation of this scale will take time. Both partners continue to work closely to support Air India's journey towards profitable growth, including strengthening structural cost efficiencies, unlocking greater synergies between Air India and Air India Express, sharpening its commercial strategy to navigate current external challenges elevating its customer proposition," SIA said in a statement.In Q2, SIA group posted a profit of Rs 1,534 crore, up from Rs 1,154 crore same period last fiscal. This was due to the stronger operating profit and a lower share of losses from associated companies, "mainly Air India (plus Rs 804 crore)."SIA describes its stake in AI group as a "key pillar of its multi-hub strategy. This direct participation in one of the world's largest and fastest growing aviation markets complements SIA Group's main hub in Singapore and broadens access to new traffic flows."Following the signing of a commercial cooperation agreement in Jan 2026, AI and SIA launched the first phase of joint initiatives this Oct. These include additional flights between Singapore and eight Indian cities and a more seamless booking experience. Enhanced reciprocal loyalty programme benefits were introduced in April 2026, with more being planned in the second quarter of 2027.The SIA group said while maintaining "disciplined cost management," it will "continue to invest strategically in both SIA and Scoot, advance its multi-hub strategy through its investment in Air India and deepen win-win partnerships with like-minded carriers in key markets."You use AI every day. articles.body: BENGALURU: Krishna Rao, Indian-origin chief financial officer of Anthropic, holds 9.4 million shares in the AI company. He is not among the shareholders selling shares in the IPO, and his shareholding will remain unchanged after the offering. The $703 million valuation is indicative and does not represent the amount he would realise from a sale, as the holding includes equity-linked awards and stock options.Rao joined Anthropic as CFO in April 2024. articles.title: Record FPI buying in November sends sensex to near 9-month high
articles.summary: MUMBAI: After more than two years, foreign funds are back buying Indian stocks.
articles.body: MUMBAI: After more than two years, foreign funds are back buying Indian stocks. In just eight trading sessions in Nov, on a net basis, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have pumped in a little over Rs 73,200 crore into Indian equities, an all-time monthly high figure that surpassed the previous record of Rs 66,135 crore in Dec 2023, data from NSDL and BSE showed.On Wednesday, FPIs net bought stocks worth Rs 12,563 crore. This, combined with the recent crash in crude prices, down about 21% this month, helped Sensex gain another 1% (773 points) to close at 81,879, nearly a nine-month high level.So far in Nov, in eight trading sessions, the bellwether index has gained 10%, about 7,400 points, and investors' wealth has jumped Rs 36 lakh crore to its highest level of Rs 510.7 lakh crore, BSE data showed. During the same period, Nifty has gained 9.7% to its Wednesday close at 25,255 points. Over the last two weeks, several factors have combined to work as tailwinds for indices, market players said.Investors’ wealth up by 4.3L crFor long, Indian companies were seen as laggards in the AI revolution that gripped some of the developed markets. As a result, several foreign fund managers took money off India to invest in AI-related stocks elsewhere. The trend is now reversing, benefitting the Indian market, brokers and analysts said.The recent US midterm poll results, seen as a rebuke to US President Donald Trump’s policies, raised prospects of a diplomatic solution to the war in West Asia, helping cool down crude prices and lower inflation expectations globally, including in India.As a result, the rupee strengthened and is up 1.3% this month to 93.7 to the dollar now. Relatively good corporate results for the July-Sept quarter (Q2FY27) also helped improve investor sentiment significantly.Siddhartha Khemka, head of research - wealth management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said Indian equities are likely to retain their positive momentum, supported by an improving earnings trajectory, a sharp correction in crude prices and a strong resurgence in foreign investors’ flows.“Q2FY27 earnings are increasingly coming in ahead of expectations, strengthening confidence in corporate earnings recovery and providing fundamental support to the ongoing rally.”Cos’ M-cap at 510.7l crIn Wednesday’s session, investors’ wealth went up by about Rs 4.3 lakh crore with the aggregate market value of companies listed on the BSE at Rs 510.7 lakh crore, an all-time high figure, exchange data showed.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nvidia reportedly preparing to oust CEO Huang after alleged affairs with spy, Nvidia exec
articles.summary: Embattled Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair.
articles.body:
Embattled Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair.

The company's board is reportedly meeting to determine if it will oust Huang as chief executive, the Wall Street Journal reports . Nvidia stock fell in after-hours trading following the report.

According to The New York Times , Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell.

She joined Nvidia in 2008 and heads up the company's healthcare business.

The Times report says that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel during a company conference in March, and that when a bystander took a photo of the interaction, a security guard "sequestered them" and made them an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement.

Last month, The Times reported that US intelligence services believed a woman, Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, may have acted as an intelligence asset , sharing information with the ruling party in Beijing.

On Sunday, Huang issued a statement apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees for having an affair, though he didn't name with whom.

In response, Nvidia's board said it is launching an independent investigation into the matter.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the board said in a statement Sunday.

She is a Boston University graduate and started her career as a hardware engineer in 1999.

articles.summary: Shares of Nvidia tanked early Wednesday evening, after The New York Times reported that CEO Jensen Huang had a second affair. Nvidia shares were trading at greater than…
articles.body:
Shares of Nvidia tanked early Wednesday evening, after The New York Times reported that CEO Jensen Huang had a second affair .

The company’s stock was down roughly 8.3 percent during after hours trading, dipping below $160 per share. Nvidia shares had not fallen below that threshold since June 2025.

Nvidia shares were trading at greater than $200 as recently as a week ago, and reached an all-time high of $243.37 on Oct. 6.

But the company’s stock has dropped since the NYT reported Huang had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang , whom U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy. Alice Huang has worked for Megaspeed , a Singaporean firm that is a customer of Nvidia.

Then on Wednesday, the paper reported on a second affair Jensen Huang had with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care.

The NYT cited five people who worked at the tech giant, whose chips power the AI industry. Jensen Huang has led Nvidia since he founded the company in 1993.

The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday evening that the company’s board, which brought in former federal prosecutor Joon H. Kim to lead an investigation into Huang, was preparing to oust the CEO.

The Hill has reached out to Nvidia for comment. The Journal reported the board is preparing to meet as soon as today regarding Jensen Huang’s future.

Jensen Huang, an ally of President Trump, acknowledged he had an affair, saying in a company memo he was “unfaithful” to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang, Bloomberg reported Sunday.

Democrats and Republicans on Capitol Hill have cited Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang as justification for restricting exports of Nvidia’s chips.

But Trump has stood by the Nvidia CEO, calling Jensen Huang an “honorable guy” on Sunday.

“I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on,” the president told reporters.

articles.title: Nvidia shares drop after hours amid reports of meeting over CEO Jensen Huang’s future
articles.summary: The New York Times reported that Huang had a relationship with an Nvidia executive following reports that he’d had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
articles.body: Shares of Nvidia dropped quickly in after-hours trading amid multiple reports that the company’s board would meet Wednesday night to discuss CEO Jensen Huang’s future after The New York Times reported that he had a relationship with an executive who reported to him. Shares fell as much as 8%. The Times report, which cited five people who worked at Nvidia, followed reports in recent days that Huang had been involved in a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. NBC News has not confirmed the Times report or reports that the company’s board was meeting Wednesday night. The Wall Street Journal first reported the board’s plans, citing people familiar with the matter. Huang wrote in a note to employees Sunday that he had been “unfaithful to his wife,” though he did not specify details. NBC News reported that officials believe the first woman, Alice Huang, was a Chinese intelligence operative. China has denied the allegations, calling them “purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China.” Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment. Nvidia’s stock drop after hours would erase almost $400 billion in value if it carries over to the regular trading session at 9:30 a.m. Thursday. Huang is among the most important people underpinning the AI boom and the trillions of dollars of investments tech giants are pouring into it around the globe. Nvidia chips are the cornerstone of the artificial intelligence boom, powering all of the top developers, from OpenAI to Anthropic. Huang founded the company and has been its leader since 1993, taking the graphics processing chip company from nothing to a valuation of more than $4 trillion.
